hero.title: Global Markets Under Pressure as Energy, Trade and Geopolitical Tensions Dominate
hero.description: Middle East energy disruption, the Trump–Xi summit, rising global bond yields, European energy security and Nigeria's Dangote Refinery are among the major stories shaping the world this morning.

breaking: 🌍 Middle East tensions continue to influence global oil and shipping markets.
🛢️ Oil remains close to the $100-a-barrel territory as markets monitor supplies and Strait of Hormuz traffic.
🇺🇸🇨🇳 Trump and Xi have held high-level talks in Washington, with trade, technology, AI, Taiwan and Iran among the major issues surrounding the summit.
📉 Global bond yields have risen sharply, with longer-term US Treasury yields reaching two-decade highs.
🇪🇺 Europe remains under pressure from higher energy and refined-product costs.
🇫🇷 Macron and Trump have discussed proposals for a moratorium on attacks against energy infrastructure in the Russia–Ukraine war.
🇳🇬 Nigeria's Dangote Refinery is becoming an increasingly important supplier of refined fuel to Europe.
📈 Strong retail interest continues around the Dangote Refinery IPO, which is testing Nigeria's digital investment infrastructure.
🇯🇵 Japan's Bank of Japan has raised its policy rate to 1.25%, its highest level in 31 years, while markets continue to watch the yen.
🌏 Asian markets are navigating higher global borrowing costs and changing expectations for interest rates.

featured.title: Trump–Xi Summit Puts Trade, Technology and Strategic Competition in Focus
featured.content: Chinese President Xi Jinping's three-day visit to the United States has brought trade, artificial intelligence, technology supply chains, Taiwan and the wider US–China relationship into focus. Trump welcomed Xi at the White House on Thursday, but Reuters reported that there was no immediate breakthrough on several difficult issues. The meeting nevertheless keeps direct communication between the two major economies at the centre of global economic diplomacy.
featured.imageQuery: Donald Trump Xi Jinping White House September 2026

world.title: Middle East Conflict Keeps Energy Markets on Edge
world.content: The conflict involving Iran continues to influence global energy markets. Oil remains around the $100-a-barrel territory, while uncertainty surrounding supplies and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz continues to affect traders. Saudi Arabia has been working to restore alternative export routes, while some flows through Hormuz have increased. Prolonged disruption could continue to affect fuel, transport, electricity and food costs worldwide.
world.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz oil tanker Middle East energy

world.title: Ukraine Energy Truce Discussions Continue
world.content: French President Emmanuel Macron has discussed with US President Donald Trump initiatives aimed at establishing a moratorium on attacks against energy infrastructure in the Russia–Ukraine war. Macron has also called for stronger defensive support for Ukraine, including additional protection against missile and drone attacks. No comprehensive new energy ceasefire has been confirmed.
world.imageQuery: Ukraine energy infrastructure winter war Kyiv

world.title: UN Diplomacy Remains Focused on Conflicts and Global Security
world.content: The United Nations General Assembly continues in New York against the backdrop of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. Energy security, artificial intelligence, international cooperation and the future of global security remain important themes as world leaders conduct meetings on the sidelines of the General Assembly.
world.imageQuery: United Nations General Assembly New York world leaders

usa.title: Trump–Xi Talks Put Trade and Technology at Centre of US–China Relations
usa.content: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping have held talks in Washington during Xi's September 23–25 visit. Trade, artificial intelligence, advanced technology, strategic supply chains, Taiwan and Iran-related issues are among the major areas surrounding the summit. Reuters reported on Thursday that there was no immediate breakthrough on several difficult issues, although the high-level dialogue keeps communication open between the two countries.
usa.imageQuery: Trump Xi Jinping White House Washington summit

usa.title: US Bond Yields Reach Multi-Year Highs
usa.content: Global financial markets are facing pressure from a broad bond sell-off. Longer-term US government bond yields have reached levels not seen for roughly two decades, increasing borrowing costs and adding pressure to equity and other financial markets. The US dollar is also heading towards a strong weekly gain as investors reassess the interest-rate outlook.
usa.imageQuery: US Treasury bonds financial markets Wall Street

europe.title: Europe Faces Renewed Energy Security Pressure
europe.content: European economies remain exposed to disruption in global energy markets. Tight supplies of refined products, including diesel and fuel oil, have pushed prices higher, while governments are balancing energy security, inflation, industrial competitiveness and household costs. Europe's dependence on imported energy remains an important issue as winter approaches.
europe.imageQuery: Europe energy crisis fuel refinery gas prices

europe.title: France Continues Discussions on Ukraine Energy Protection
europe.content: France remains involved in diplomatic efforts concerning protection of Ukrainian energy infrastructure. President Emmanuel Macron said he discussed with Donald Trump the possibility of a moratorium on energy-related attacks between Russia and Ukraine and stressed the need for stronger defensive protection for Ukraine.

africa.title: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery Gains Importance in European Fuel Market
africa.content: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery is attracting growing international attention as Middle East disruptions reshape global fuel trade. Reuters reported that the refinery has emerged as an important supplier of refined fuel to Europe during the current supply disruption. The development highlights Nigeria's growing role in international refined petroleum markets.

africa.title: Nigeria's Fuel Prices Remain Under Pressure
africa.content: Nigeria continues to face pressure from higher international oil prices. Reuters reported earlier this week that petrol prices had reached around 1,400 naira per litre in Lagos and Abuja and about 1,500 naira in some northern locations, while diesel prices had exceeded 2,000 naira in some markets. The Dangote Refinery has been operating at high capacity, but international crude costs continue to influence domestic fuel prices.
africa.imageQuery: Nigeria petrol station fuel prices Lagos

africa.title: Dangote IPO Attracts Strong Retail Interest
africa.content: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO continues to attract significant attention from Nigerian retail investors. Reuters reported that several digital investment platforms experienced outages as investors rushed to participate. The offering is therefore also highlighting both the growing interest in Nigeria's capital markets and the capacity of digital investment infrastructure to handle large volumes of retail demand. Strong public interest does not guarantee future investment returns.
africa.imageQuery: Dangote refinery IPO Nigeria investors stock market

business.title: Global Bond Sell-Off Raises Borrowing Costs
business.content: Global bond markets are under pressure as longer-term government yields rise across major economies. Reuters reported that US yields reached two-decade highs during the latest market sell-off. Higher yields can increase financing costs for governments, companies and households and can also place pressure on equity valuations.

business.title: Global Diesel Supply Remains Tight
business.content: The global diesel market remains under pressure as conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine disrupt supply chains. Reuters reported that tight inventories and disrupted refining flows could keep diesel supplies constrained into 2027. The situation is important because diesel is central to road transport, agriculture, manufacturing and logistics.
business.imageQuery: diesel fuel refinery tanker global energy market

technology.title: US–China AI Competition Remains a Global Issue
technology.content: Artificial intelligence remains a central element of US–China strategic competition. Both countries are pursuing stronger domestic technology ecosystems while also discussing AI safety and the management of technology-related risks. Trade restrictions, advanced chips, supply chains and AI development are increasingly interconnected with international economic policy.
technology.imageQuery: artificial intelligence semiconductor technology China USA

asia.title: Japan Raises Interest Rates to 31-Year High
asia.content: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25% on September 18, its highest level in 31 years. Markets remain focused on whether further increases will follow and on the impact of monetary policy on the Japanese yen, inflation and economic activity.
asia.imageQuery: Bank of Japan Tokyo financial district yen

asia.title: Asian Markets Navigate Global Bond Sell-Off
asia.content: Asian markets are navigating higher global borrowing costs as the international bond sell-off pushes longer-term US yields to two-decade highs. Investors are also watching currency movements, interest-rate expectations and the continuing impact of elevated energy prices.

morningSummary: Good morning and welcome to RadiantWaves Media. Global markets are beginning the day under pressure from geopolitical tensions, higher energy costs and a major bond-market sell-off. The Trump–Xi summit in Washington remains a major international focus, while the Middle East conflict continues to influence oil and shipping markets. Europe is dealing with energy-security concerns, France remains involved in discussions over protecting Ukrainian energy infrastructure, and Nigeria's Dangote Refinery is gaining a larger role in international fuel markets.
bigQuestion: As energy, technology and geopolitical tensions increasingly affect everyday life, are countries becoming more economically dependent on one another despite growing strategic competition?
